chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, and others, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them).
Regarding a man who retracted from Islam, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is asked to repent, so if he repents (it is fine), or else he is killed.'

key_terms.يُسْتَتَابُ: He is asked to repent / Given time to repent

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on an apostate who retracts from Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the foundational Shia legal procedure of *istitabah* (granting a period of repentance) before executing an apostate, distinguishing it from the Sunni view of immediate execution. It highlights the juristic principle that apostasy is treated as a temporary state of disbelief that can be rectified through sincere reversion to Islam, thereby preserving the individual's life and status within the community.
